judgment.rationale: Both are P2 Skills Objectives in the same grain under Unit 2 'Numbers from 0 to 500' (Key Unit Competence: count, read, write, arrange, compare, add/subtract, multiply and divide whole numbers 0-500), so the statement-type and rank coordinate (P2, rank 1) are identical and same-rank direction rests on substantive content. Proficiency in the numeration objective therefore supports likely success in the division objective; the reverse support is not evidenced. Shared Unit/Topic Area ancestry and the single overlapping LC token 'numbers' were treated as nomination signals only, not as the basis of this judgment. First: '– Draw a square, a rectangle, a triangle, and a circle.' (Unit 11, Sub-Topic 'Geometrical Figures and a Circle'; LCs 'Draw a square/rectangle/triangle/circle'). Source anchors also place the selection objective (table row 5) before the drawing objective (row 6). Proficiency in visual identification therefore supports success in accurate construction, not the reverse.
